bull.b: The Anthropic agreement materially improves revenue visibility and diversifies TeraWulf toward contracted AI infrastructure. Its long duration and large capacity commitment can support sustained utilization, financing access and platform expansion as additional phases are delivered.

bull.t: Expanding HPC capacity and lease revenue
bull.b: Rapid HPC lease growth and commissioning progress indicate a transition from mainly development activity toward recurring infrastructure revenue. CB-4 and CB-5 additions should expand the operating base, while the company targets further contracted critical IT capacity.

Substantial liquidity and proceeds from monetizing Abernathy give TeraWulf resources to fund committed construction and redeploy capital into larger, controlled campuses. This supports execution flexibility and reduces reliance on immediate equity-market funding.

bear.b: The company has not yet converted strong gross margins or growing infrastructure revenue into sustainable operating earnings. Large losses and negative adjusted EBITDA may persist while new capacity is pre-revenue, limiting internally funded growth and increasing financing dependence.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and weak capitalization
bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow show that the business remains capital intensive and is not self-funding. Reported zero equity and historically high debt relative to equity weaken financial flexibility, leaving the company exposed to refinancing, dilution or project-funding risk.

Scaling complex campuses depends on scarce electrical labor and customer-driven design work, creating schedule risk. Until new capacity reaches service, low reported margins and substantial interest outflows can constrain cash conversion and delay progress toward target economics.
